paragraphs.text: See on Eze 2:1.
paragraphs.anchor: And thou, son of man.

paragraphs.text: This was the King of Babylon. {as Isa 7:20} The Turk is at this day such another. Mohammed I was, in his time, the death of 800,000 men. Selymus II, in revenge of the loss received at Lepanto, would have put to death all the Christians in his dominions. {a}
paragraphs.anchor: Take thee a sharp knife.

paragraphs.text: Take thee a barber’s razor.] Not a "deceitful razor," {as Psa 52:2} but one that will do the deed - sharp and sure. Pliny {b} telleth us, out of Varo, that the Romans had no barbers till 454 years after the city was built; ante intonsi fuere.

As hairs are an ornament to the head and beard, so are people to a city. But, as when they begin to be a burden or trouble to either, they are cut off and cast away; so are people by God’s judgments, when by their sins they are offensive to him; dealing as Dionysius did by his god Aesculapius, from whom he presumed to pull his golden beard. David felt himself shaved in his ambassadors; so doth God in his servants - whose very hairs are numbered {Mat 10:30} - in his ministers especially - who, by a specialty, are called God’s men {1Ti 6:11 2Ti 3:17} - with whom to meddle is more dangerous than to take a lion by the beard or a bear by the hair.
paragraphs.anchor: And cause it to pass upon thy head and upon thy beard.

paragraphs.text: This showeth that God’s judgments are just to a hair’s weight: and capillus unus suam habet umbram, saith Mimus.
paragraphs.anchor: Then take the balances to weigh.

paragraphs.text: Dii nos quasi pilas habent, saith Plautus; Imo quasi pilos, saith another.
paragraphs.anchor: And divide the hair.

paragraphs.text: {a} Turkish History, 885.
{b} Lib. vii. cap. 59.

i.e., With famine, pestilence, and other mischiefs, during the siege of Jerusalem. Pythagoras gave this precept among others, Unguium, criniumque praesegmina ne contemnito. But God findeth so little worth in wicked people that he regardeth them not, but casteth them as excrements to the dunghill, yea, to hell. {Psa 9:17}
paragraphs.anchor: Thou shalt burn with fire a third part

paragraphs.text: They shall be slain with that sharp knife or sword, {Eze 5:1} after that the city is taken.
paragraphs.anchor: And smite about it with a knife.

paragraphs.text: Sundry of them shall flee for their lives; but in running from death they shall but run to it. {Amo 9:1-4; Amo 2:13-16}
paragraphs.anchor: Thou shalt scatter in the wind.

paragraphs.text: A remnant is still reserved, "that the Lord God may dwell among men." {Psa 68:18} See Jer 44:28 2Ki 25:12 Isa 1:9; Isa 6:10.
paragraphs.anchor: Thou shalt also take thereof a few in number.

paragraphs.text: Thus "evil shall hunt a wicked man to overthrow him"; {Psa 140:11} {See Trapp on "Psa 140:11"} he shall not escape, though he hath escaped; his preservation is but a reservation to further mischief, except he repent.
paragraphs.anchor: Then take of them again, and cast them into the midst of the fire.

paragraphs.text: Such he meaneth as were combustible matter; for there were a sort of precious ones among them, who being brought by God through the fire, were thereby "refined as silver is refined, and tried as gold is tried." {Zec 13:9} {See Trapp on "Zec 13:9"}
paragraphs.anchor: And burn them in the fire.

paragraphs.text: i.e., This head and beard so to be shaved. {Eze 5:1} By the hair of the head some think the wise men of that city are figured out, and by the hair of the beard are the strong men; the razor of God’s severity maketh clean work, leaving no stub or stump behind it.
paragraphs.anchor: This is Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: As the head, heart, and centre of the earth. See Psa 72:10 Eze 38:12; and God had peculiar ends in it, that the law might go forth out of Zion, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem, and that all nations might flow into it. {Isa 2:2-3} Talis est Roma Christianis, Such now is Rome to Christians, saith A Lapide; but lay a straw there, say we; or, as the Gloss saith upon some decrees of popes, Haec non credo, I believe it not. See Rev 17:5.
paragraphs.anchor: I have set it in the midst of the nations.

paragraphs.text: This was a foul change; this was to do evil as she could; {Jer 3:5} this was ingratitude of the worst sort, such as Socrates called ειλικρινη αδικιαν, manifest injustice. Such a wretched change is complained of, Jer 2:11 Rom 1:23; Rom 1:25 Jdg 1:4, but nowhere in so high an expression as this, as one observeth.
paragraphs.anchor: And she hath changed my judgments into wickedness.

paragraphs.text: Because the Jews had better laws but worse dispositions than they.
paragraphs.anchor: More than the nations.

paragraphs.text: scil., Your transgressions and superstitions, or because ye have abounded with blessings, and made me so ill a requital. Some render it Quia tumultuastis vos plus quam vicinae gentes; and indeed there were many murders committed among them, and many revolts from foreign princes whom they had sworn to serve.
paragraphs.anchor: Because ye multiplied

paragraphs.text: But have outsinned them, qui deos suos quamvis viles et multos non mutant, who change not their gods (as you have done me, Jer 2:10-11), but follow the natural light of reason (some of them at least do so, Rom 2:14), which you have debauched. See 1Co 5:1 Eze 16:46-48.
paragraphs.anchor: Neither have done according to the judgment of the nations.

paragraphs.text: Whether thou wilt believe it or not. Thou boldest it unlikely, but shalt find it true, and that I am very serious, not saying these things in terrorem only. Ecce me adversum te venientem, so some render it; Behold I am upon my march against thee, and will punish thee surely, severely, suddenly.
paragraphs.anchor: Behold, I, even I, am against thee.

paragraphs.text: For the non-execution of my judgments in the former sense taken. {as Eze 5:7}
paragraphs.anchor: And will execute judgments.

paragraphs.text: In whose sight thou hast so sinned, and who will rejoice at thy sufferings.
paragraphs.anchor: In the sight of the nations.

paragraphs.text: None shall suffer so much here or sink so deep in hell, as a profane Jew, a carnal gospeller, who is therefore worse than others, because he ought to be better. Oh, the height and weight of those judgments that shall be heaped upon such! See Lam 4:6.
paragraphs.anchor: And I will do in thee that which I have not done.

paragraphs.text: For where ever read we that the fathers did eat their sons in an open visible way? and the sons the Fathers?
paragraphs.anchor: And whereunto I will not do any more the like.

paragraphs.text: See this fulfilled in the pitiful mothers; {Lam 4:10} and may it be thought, saith one, that their hungry husbands shared not with them in those viands? Oh, the severity of God. Cavebis, si pavebis.
paragraphs.anchor: Therefore the fathers shall eat the sons.

paragraphs.text: A miserably dejected people the Jews are to this day, banished out of the world, as it were, by a common consent of nations.
paragraphs.anchor: And the whole remnant of thee will I scatter.

paragraphs.text: This is God’s usual oath (in this prophet especially), and therefore should not be used as an oath or asseveration by any other, since he only liveth (to speak properly).
paragraphs.anchor: Wherefore, as I live, saith the Lord.

paragraphs.text: Or, I will break thee down; or, I will shave thee. {as Eze 5:1 Jer 48:37}
paragraphs.anchor: Therefore will I also diminish thee.

paragraphs.text: See Eze 5:2.
paragraphs.anchor: A third part of thee, &c.

paragraphs.text: God is then said to be angry when he doth what men do when angry - viz. (1.) Chide; (2.) Smite.
paragraphs.anchor: Then shall mine anger be accomplished.

paragraphs.text: This also is spoken after the manner of men, who are much comforted when they can be avenged. Their song is, Oh, how sweet is revenge!
paragraphs.anchor: And I will be comforted.

paragraphs.text: “ Animumque explesse iuvabit. ” - Virgil

The same word in Hebrew that signifieth vengeance, signifieth comfort also; for God will be comforted in the execution of his wrath. But what a venomous and vile thing is sin, that causeth the most merciful God to take comfort in the destruction of his creature!
That is, seriously threatened by my prophets, whom they have vilipended and derided, but shall now feel the weight of their words.
paragraphs.anchor: And they shall know that I the Lord have spoken it in my zeal.

paragraphs.text: This he doth not usually all at once, but by degrees. He suffereth not his whole wrath to arise till there be no remedy. {as 2Ch 36:16}
paragraphs.anchor: When I have accomplished my fury in them.

paragraphs.text: In ariditatem, a dry and barren wilderness, whose fruitfulness and pleasantness is so much celebrated, not only by divine, but profane authors also. See Psa 107:34. {See Trapp on "Psa 107:34"}
paragraphs.anchor: Moreover, I will make thee waste.

paragraphs.text: See on Eze 5:8.
paragraphs.anchor: In the sight of all.

paragraphs.text: See this fulfilled, Lam 2:15-16.
paragraphs.anchor: So it shall be a reproach and taunt.

paragraphs.text: They shall enjoy thy folly, grow wise by thy harms. I will make thee an example to the heathen. {a}
paragraphs.anchor: An instruction.

paragraphs.text: A terror, some render it.
paragraphs.anchor: An astonishment.

paragraphs.text: {a} Exemplum. - Vulg.
Not to warn you, as Jonathan’s arrows did David, but to wound you to the heart, and to lay you heaps upon heaps. {Deu 32:23-24}
paragraphs.anchor: When I shall send upon you the evil arrows of famine.

paragraphs.text: See Eze 4:16. Penuria fiet pecuniae, saith Oecolampadius here; You shall want money to buy you bread.
paragraphs.anchor: And break your staff of bread.

paragraphs.text: Rob thee of thy children, destroy thy cattle, make thee few in number, and thy highway desolate, as was long before threatened. {Lev 26:22 2Ki 17:25}
paragraphs.anchor: Evil beasts, and they shall bereave thee.

paragraphs.text: I Jehovah, who will give being to my menaces as well as to my promises.
paragraphs.anchor: I the Lord have spoken it.
